knowledge.title: Dual-GPU device loss and separate benchmark harness failure

records.statement: After heavy simultaneous SDXL, nvidia-smi reported GPU is lost and fresh PyTorch exposed only the RTX 4090.
Windows historical PnP visibility, live PCIe enumeration, NVML visibility, and CUDA usability are separate diagnostic layers.
After true cold boot both devices were Windows OK / ProblemCode 0, visible to nvidia-smi and CUDA/PyTorch; P100 idle was approximately 9 MiB and 0% utilization.
The P100 passed FP32 CUDA work, simultaneous bounded CUDA work, local LLM inference, partial 32B offload, batched inference, and compatible all-FP16 SDXL output; bad hardware is not proven.
The root cause of device loss is unresolved; driver, PCIe, motherboard/chipset, PSU, workload, and runtime contributors remain competing hypotheses.
P100 hardware failure is not established as the cause.
Successful independent and simultaneous P100 workloads contradict treating the P100 as proven bad hardware, while device loss contradicts assuming the healthy baseline persisted.
Stopping stale workers, a fresh CUDA process, device rescan, and warm reboot did not restore the P100.
A true cold electrical power cycle restored P100 PCIe/PnP/NVML/CUDA enumeration.
Post-cycle evidence showed both devices CM_PROB_NONE, nvidia-smi visibility, and PyTorch GPU count 2.
If device loss survives user-space cleanup, rescan, and warm reboot, stop heavy stress reproduction and escalate for forensic analysis.
The 0x133 DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION remains unresolved; WinDbg analysis of MEMORY.DMP and the minidump is the next forensic step.
A separate benchmark-harness failure produced WinError 1224 when an image viewer held a canonical PNG open or memory-mapped.
The harness was corrected to write unique per-run files and copy successful output to canonical names; this failure class is distinct from CUDA/P100 device loss.
Do not intentionally reproduce the watchdog crash or perform mass local-AI population during this infrastructure slice.
